raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fix #33828.

The `run_mistral3()` example in `vision_language_offline.py` crashes with:
```
RuntimeError: Expected there to be 1 prompt placeholders corresponding to 1 image items, but instead found 0 prompt placeholders!
```

Root cause: `[IMG]` is tokenized into regular subword tokens, not Mistral's special image token (ID 10). Pixtral's processor sets `target=""` + `is_update_applied=True`, meaning it never does placeholder replacement — it assumes image tokens were already inserted by the Mistral tokenizer during chat encoding.

Fix: Following the pattern in `mistral-small_offline.py`, switch to `llm.chat()` + `tokenizer_mode="mistral"` so the native Mistral tokenizer handles image token insertion. No changes to vLLM core — only adds a `use_llm_chat` branch in the example harness. Trade-off: Mistral3 now takes a different path from the other ~70 models in this file.

## Test Plan

Verified preprocessing behavior in Docker (vllm v0.20.0, GPU):
- Raw `[IMG]` + HF tokenizer → RuntimeError (confirms bug exists)
- Mistral tokenizer + chat template → preprocessing succeeds
- `ruff check` passes

## Test Result

```
Test 1: raw [IMG] + HF tokenizer...
  PASS - got expected RuntimeError
Test 2: Mistral tokenizer + chat template...
  PASS - preprocessing succeeded
```

## Notes
- No existing open PR addresses this issue.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces support for using the high-level LLM chat API (`llm.chat`) in the offline vision-language example when `use_llm_chat` is enabled, specifically updating the Mistral 3 configuration to utilize this mode. A review comment points out that using the raw `data` object directly bypasses image modifications (like repeat probability) and silently ignores cache hit verification. It suggests raising an error for unsupported cache verification and extracting the processed images from `inputs` instead.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

When `use_llm_chat` is enabled, the code currently uses the original `data` image directly. This bypasses any image modifications (such as pixel changes) made by `apply_image_repeat` when `--image-repeat-prob` is specified. Additionally, `--verify-mm-cache-hit-with-uuids` is silently ignored because the function returns early before the verification block is reached. We should raise an error if cache hit verification is requested (as it is not supported via the high-level chat API) and use the images from `inputs` to respect the repeat probability.
